children: Bank of America kept its Buy rating on CoreWeave
on Thursday after a roughly 18% drop in the last two sessions as it raised their revenue forecasts. Stock was down ~2% at $64.47.
"The decline in share price yesterday likely reflects concerns over financing hurdles for AI infrastructure players," said analyst Tal Liani.

The analysts held their price target at $140, based on a price of 26 times expected 2027 operating profit, above the 14 to 19 times the analysts apply to peer cloud data center companies because of CoreWeave’s faster expected growth.

BofA now expects CoreWeave’s revenue to grow 105% in 2027 and 63% in 2028, up from earlier forecasts of 102% and 58%. It projects revenue of $26.5B in 2027 and $43.3B in 2028, up from $26B and $41B. For 2026, it projects $12.9B.

BofA expects CoreWeave to add 1.4 to 1.5 gigawatts of active power capacity annually over the next two years, while revenue per megawatt could rise to about $14 by the end of 2028 from roughly $10 currently, partly as the company begins using Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin chips.

BofA also raised its spending forecasts to $47.4B in 2027 and $49.8B in 2028, from $43.8B and $44.7B. It estimated that CoreWeave will spend about $23.8B more cash than it takes in this year and $24.8B more in 2027. It estimated the company’s debt at about three times its shareholder equity at the end of 2026.

CoreWeave’s contracted backlog stands at at least $129B. Most of its customers are large technology companies with strong credit ratings, and the company typically signs five-year deals, which the analysts said helps it borrow at lower cost. Meta
accounts for $35B of the backlog, and OpenAI
made up 66% of the backlog at the end of 2024 and less than 33% a year later.

title: BofA keeps Buy on CoreWeave after stock drop, sees higher revenue
